existing_findings.condition: A fault whose ID, count and adjacent-point checks pass, with a public/derived-Serde TravelGeometryPoint containing an axis value outside WGS84 bounds, can reach longitude()/latitude() inside the fault validation predicates. Those methods reconstruct a checked axis and expect success, allowing a panic rather than a returned validation error. Integer maximum is within i32 representation but outside latitude and longitude E7 limits.
existing_findings.limits: No malformed world or terrain pack, deserializer path, producer, validator call or panic executed. Earlier predicate short-circuit may reject a specific fault before reaching the invalid point; practical malformed input admission and load ordering need separately established. Related country/map/routing callers remain independently scoped.
existing_findings.future_repair_direction: After complete audit and authorization, decide accepted coordinate owner/decoding and propagate malformed-coordinate failure through these validators without conflating WGS84 and projected coordinates.

existing_findings.classification: Existing 059 mapped-geology source/projection/containment question; independently traced bounded producer and consumer, no new count
existing_findings.condition: Importer constructs rounded rectangles only after geometry point and polygon-window containment checks; raw MappedGeologicWindow public/Serde values are later checked for nonempty ID and positive size <=2000 m, not compared to a source polygon. Mapped-lithology projects a 3×3 sample set expanded by a fixed 2 m margin and requires every sample in one window.
existing_findings.limits: This source-only review does not prove that the native geometry predicate or projection is wrong, that any finite 2 m margin fails, that raw windows can enter a supported authenticated package, or that the whole projected footprint is certified. Source provenance, validation authority and a bound on the unsampled continuum remain open.
existing_findings.future_repair_direction: After audit/authorization, establish actual source/package admission and projection enclosure policy and preserve missing-coverage semantics.

open_policy_questions.question: Candidates are ordered by source fid; after the first containing feature, missing mapped lithology or failure of all trial windows returns None instead of trying later overlapping candidates. Is first-feature precedence intentional when a later feature could provide coverage?

nonfindings: The geology variant geometry() returns an empty slice intentionally; do not impose the two-point fault trace rule on it.
Window i32 coordinates widen before subtraction and f64 comparison; NaN projected point comparisons do not satisfy contains.
Normal no-coverage is represented as None and leaves source heightfield behavior as documented; missing lithology is not by itself evidence of a bug.
Compiler source includes polygon/rectangle contains calls, rather than just comparing four corners; native geo implementation and product behavior were not independently executed or certified.
Inspected test source describes expectations only and no tests were run.

How are polygon geometry provenance, projected coordinate values and unit/lithology bound to the signed or otherwise authenticated input package?
Under the supported projection, geographic domain and all caller footprint radii, is the nine-point plus 2 m check sufficient for the complete footprint?
Does first-containing-feature precedence intentionally suppress later valid overlapping windows?
What are actual decoded count/allocation limits and generic error ownership before point aggregation?
All other source families, original checkpoint 3821, full thirteen-lens completion and connected global aliases remain open.

lenses.name: producer-propagation
lenses.bounded_assessment: Importer chooses a containing polygon and mapped lithology, emits a window, world and pack validators perform field checks, and mapped_lithology consumes projection samples. Neither validator re-establishes original polygon provenance.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens

lenses.name: existing-type-owners
lenses.bounded_assessment: GeologicUnitId and SurfaceLithology are typed values; coordinates in window are projected EPSG:3034 while fault points use WGS84 E7. Do not replace one coordinate space or evidence role with another solely because both use numeric pairs.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens

lenses.name: admission-contracts
lenses.bounded_assessment: Fault validation calls checked-coordinate getters on public derived-Serde raw i32 points, and those getters expect valid WGS84 values. If earlier checks pass and an out-of-axis point is reached, the existing F007 dependency permits panic rather than a validation error.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens

lenses.name: invariant-operations
lenses.bounded_assessment: Window extent is widened from i32 to i64 before subtraction; signed endpoint differences are representable. Fault point counts sum as usize before the total budget comparison; actual input/allocation limits remain open and no overflow witness is claimed.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens

lenses.name: aggregate-states
lenses.bounded_assessment: Strict ID order and geometry budgets apply across feature variants; fault traces need two distinct-adjacent points while geology intentionally has no trace and its own window validity predicate. Polygon provenance is a separate aggregate property.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens

lenses.name: type-ownership
lenses.bounded_assessment: The source contains shared TerrainFeature, its public variant payloads, private pack validation and a separate world-import validator. Decide authority and error ownership across construction/import/pack/consumption before imposing one representation.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens

lenses.name: redundant-authority
lenses.bounded_assessment: Import and terrain pack repeat related field validation, with distinct bounds and build-report checks. Independently review drift and intentional policy differences; this comparison does not prove they should be collapsed.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens

lenses.name: behavior-preservation
lenses.bounded_assessment: Preserve optional no-coverage behavior, fault-versus-geology variant rules, projected/geographic coordinate distinction and source-prior semantics. Test source records intentions only, not execution evidence.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens

lenses.name: enum-shapes
lenses.bounded_assessment: MappedFault and MappedGeology are payload-owning enum variants; activity booleans document modern mapped attributes and do not claim historical activity. No shape defect asserted by field names.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens

lenses.name: derivability
lenses.bounded_assessment: Both schema payloads and enum already derive Serde/Clone/Eq as appropriate; derivation denies unknown fields but does not seal public aggregate invariants. No mechanical derive change justified in bounded scope.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens

lenses.name: type-granularity
lenses.bounded_assessment: Feature IDs, lithology, unit IDs, axis-bounded WGS84 coordinates and projected rectangle endpoints have distinct semantics; one shared comparison on id does not prove a unified namespace owner or provenance.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens

lenses.name: magic-strings
lenses.bounded_assessment: Feature IDs are external strings ordered together; importer formats an egdi-window prefix and anchor. Existing Q-L12-55045c36a6ef2b4f0ffd asks for mapped geology source, projection and admission; source namespace and collision policy remain open.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens

lenses.name: magic-numbers
lenses.bounded_assessment: Named 4096 per-fault, 100000 geometry points, 50000 windows and 2000 m window side are resource/policy bounds, not defects by themselves. Nine sample points and 2 m projection margin need an actual enclosure argument over supported footprints.
lenses.closure: not assessed for the whole lens
